summary:
We developed **SPHEREx Explorer**, a web-based astronomical data visualization and analysis platform that processes and presents large-scale observational datasets from NASA's SPHEREx space telescope. The system integrates astronomical data retrieval, coordinate-based spatial filtering, image processing, and interactive sky visualization. A key technical challenge was handling computationally intensive astronomical datasets, including FITS image data, extracting relevant metadata, and efficiently processing observations based on parameters such as Right Ascension, Declination, wavelength bands, and observation regions. We developed a pipeline to retrieve, filter, and process relevant observations while minimizing unnecessary data transfer and computational overhead. The platform also aims to support interactive sky navigation, allowing users to select regions of the celestial sphere and map their positions to astronomical coordinates for targeted data retrieval and analysis.

By combining backend data processing with an interactive frontend, SPHEREx Explorer makes computationally complex astronomical observations more accessible. It provides a foundation for scalable astronomical exploration, enabling researchers, students, and astronomy enthusiasts to investigate large volumes of space telescope data without requiring specialized data-processing infrastructure.
details:
Project Details – SPHEREx Explorer

SPHEREx Explorer is an interactive astronomical exploration and data-analysis platform built around NASA's SPHEREx space telescope. Its primary objective is to simplify access to large-scale astronomical observations while providing computational tools to identify and investigate potentially interesting celestial objects and their movement across multiple observations.

The platform retrieves observational metadata, identifies relevant SPHEREx observations, and processes astronomical FITS images for further analysis. A major component is its image-processing pipeline, which compares observations taken at different times to identify potential moving celestial objects. It uses image-shift correction, Gaussian-based subpixel centroid estimation, uncertainty calculations, and statistical displacement scoring to distinguish genuine movement from noise and image-alignment errors. This is particularly important because astronomical objects may shift by fractions of a pixel between observations.

The platform is also designed around an interactive sky-exploration interface, incorporating celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination), observation footprints, image inspection, and region-based exploration. Users can explore specific regions of the sky and retrieve corresponding observational data.

Technical tools and technologies:

  • Python: Backend processing, astronomical data handling, and computational pipelines.
  • FITS image processing: Handling and analysing astronomical observation images.
  • FastAPI: Backend API architecture for connecting data processing with the frontend.
  • React / Next.js: Frontend development and interactive user interface.
  • Statistical image analysis: Centroid estimation, image registration, uncertainty modelling, and displacement significance testing.
  • SPHEREx observational data: Primary source of astronomical observations and metadata.
  • HTML: Generating visual reports of detected candidate regions.

Creativity and innovation: The project goes beyond simply displaying telescope images. It attempts to transform astronomical archives into an interactive discovery environment, combining spatial exploration, computational image analysis, and multi-epoch observation comparison. One of its envisioned features is a Street View-like experience for exploring the night sky, where users can select a region of the celestial sphere and retrieve the corresponding astronomical observations.

Factors considered: We considered the computational cost of processing large FITS files, image resolution, memory consumption, coordinate accuracy, observation alignment, false-positive detection, statistical confidence, data accessibility, and scalability.

Intended impact: SPHEREx Explorer aims to make advanced astronomical datasets more accessible, reduce the technical barriers to astronomical research, and provide an extensible platform for identifying moving celestial objects and exploring the universe through real observational data.
